article: Win32 button control and WM_COMMAND event handling
scope: Compared the full Japanese source and twelve translations, C++ sample code, event semantics, control ID handling, source repository, metadata dates, and official Microsoft references.
findings: Removed duplicate future date; retained 2023-01-14 and set lastmod to 2026-11-24.
Corrected the Japanese typo for GUI control and rewrote the sample as a window-procedure fragment with button creation in WM_CREATE.
Added the BN_CLICKED test and retained the control ID test because WM_COMMAND can also originate from menus and accelerators.
Used a pointer-sized HMENU conversion and checked CreateWindow failure.
Added official Microsoft Learn references and disclosed that the linked external GitHub sample still lacks the BN_CLICKED filter.

post/ボタンついて/index.en.md.summary: Compared the complete Japanese article and all twelve translations against Microsoft Win32 documentation. Corrected event handling to filter BN_CLICKED as well as the control ID, showed button creation in WM_CREATE, clarified WM_COMMAND message fields, and disclosed that the linked original repository still contains the unfiltered handler.

meaning.note: Compared button creation, parent-window notification, close action, and the distinction between a click notification and other WM_COMMAND sources.

terminology.note: Verified Win32 button control, WM_CREATE, WM_COMMAND, BN_CLICKED, LOWORD/HIWORD, control ID, parent window, and instance handle.

code.note: Rewrote the code fragment to define an ID, create the child button during WM_CREATE, check both ID_BUTTON1 and BN_CLICKED, handle CreateWindow failure, and use pointer-sized HMENU conversion.

links.note: Added Microsoft Learn references for button styles, BN_CLICKED, WM_COMMAND, and window creation; inspected the linked GitHub source and disclosed its current missing BN_CLICKED filter.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.
The linked GitHub repository is external to this site repository and was not modified; its current main.cpp still handles WM_COMMAND by control ID without checking BN_CLICKED.
The displayed C++ is a relevant window-procedure fragment, not a complete standalone application.
